## Load packages

`fgsea` and `enrichVolcano` (not on CRAN) are called with `::`.

```{r setup}
pacman::p_load(
  here, dplyr, tibble, tidyr, purrr, limma, ggplot2, patchwork, readxl, writexl
)
here::i_am("03_Pathway_Enrichment/01_run_fgsea_and_fry/a_script/01_run_fgsea_and_fry.qmd")
```

## Read inputs

Every tested set is checked on every contrast with two methods. fgsea ranks proteins by a
statistic and asks whether a set's members sit towards either end of the ranking more than random
sets of the same size. It is competitive and assumes proteins are exchangeable, which they are
not: proteins in a pathway move together. limma's fry is self-contained: it asks whether the set's
members move at all, from the sample-level data, so correlation between members cannot inflate its
null.

```{r read}
stage <- here("03_Pathway_Enrichment", "01_run_fgsea_and_fry")
gene_sets <- here("03_Pathway_Enrichment", "00_build_gene_sets", "c_data")
sets <- readRDS(file.path(gene_sets, "gene_sets.rds"))
gene_set_book <- file.path(gene_sets, "00_build_gene_sets.xlsx")
set_catalog <- read_excel(gene_set_book, "set_catalog")
protein_map <- read_excel(gene_set_book, "protein_gene_map")
fit <- readRDS(here("02_Differential_Expression", "02_Differential", "c_data", "fit.rds"))
d <- readRDS(here("02_Differential_Expression", "01_Design", "c_data", "design.rds"))
proteins <- readRDS(here("01_Preprocess", "02_Quantification", "c_data", "proteins.rds"))
```

## Check alignment

A stale fit still lines up by count, so the checks compare names.

```{r check}
contrast_names <- colnames(d$contrasts)
stopifnot(
  identical(rownames(fit$coefficients), protein_map$protein),
  identical(colnames(fit$coefficients), contrast_names),
  identical(rownames(proteins$E), protein_map$protein),
  identical(rownames(d$design), colnames(proteins$E))
)
```

## Protein results

One `topTable()` row per protein and contrast, BH within each contrast as in `02_Differential`.
`pi_score` is P.Value^|logFC| (Xiao et al. 2014, PMID 22321699); it orders proteins and selects
nothing.

```{r protein-results}
protein_results <- map(set_names(contrast_names), function(contrast) {
  topTable(fit, coef = contrast, number = Inf, sort.by = "none") |>
    rownames_to_column("protein") |>
    select(protein, logFC, AveExpr, t, P.Value, adj.P.Val)
}) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "contrast") |>
  left_join(protein_map, by = "protein", relationship = "many-to-one") |>
  mutate(pi_score = P.Value^abs(logFC))
```

```{r protein-summary}
protein_summary <- protein_results |>
  summarise(
    tested = n(),
    up = sum(adj.P.Val < 0.05 & logFC > 0),
    down = sum(adj.P.Val < 0.05 & logFC < 0),
    min_fdr = signif(min(adj.P.Val), 3), .by = contrast
  )
protein_summary
```

## Run fgsea

fgsea ranks the moderated t of each representative protein, named by gene symbol so leading
edges come back as symbols. The seeded calls draw their permutations in the order of `ranked`.

```{r ranked}
ranked <- map(set_names(contrast_names), function(cn) {
  with(filter(protein_results, selected, contrast == cn), set_names(t, gene))
})
```

`padj` is BH over all sets in the contrast. NES (normalised enrichment score) is positive when
members sit towards the top of the ranking. The leading edge is the members that drive the score.

```{r fgsea}
set.seed(1)
fgsea_raw <- map(ranked, function(stats) fgsea::fgsea(sets, stats, minSize = 15, maxSize = 500))
```

## Run fry

fry reads rows of `proteins$E`, so set symbols become row numbers through each representative
protein. It reads limpa's precision weights from `proteins$weights`, with robust empirical Bayes
and the design of the protein fit, blood index included. No `block`: participant is a fixed term,
which leaves little within-leg correlation (`correlation_strata` sheet of `01_Design`).

```{r fry-index}
selected_rows <- which(protein_map$selected)
set_rows <- map(sets, function(genes) {
  selected_rows[match(genes, protein_map$gene[selected_rows])]
})
proteins$weights <- fit$EList$weights
```

One row per set, contrast and method. fgsea's `padj` and fry's `FDR` are each package's own BH;
neither is recomputed.

```{r set-tests}
set_tests <- bind_rows(
  map(contrast_names, function(contrast) {
    as_tibble(fgsea_raw[[contrast]]) |>
      transmute(
        set_id = pathway, contrast, method = "fgsea", n = size,
        direction = if_else(NES > 0, "Up", "Down"), NES, p = pval, padj,
        leadingEdge
      )
  }),
  map(contrast_names, function(contrast) {
    fry(proteins, set_rows, d$design, d$contrasts[, contrast], robust = TRUE, sort = "none") |>
      rownames_to_column("set_id") |>
      transmute(
        set_id, contrast,
        method = "fry", n = NGenes,
        direction = Direction, NES = NA_real_, p = PValue, padj = FDR,
        leadingEdge = list(NULL)
      )
  })
)
table(set_tests$method)
```

## Collapse redundant sets

Collections overlap: glycolysis sits in all four. `fgsea::collapsePathways()` walks the
significant sets in order of p; each set not yet a child acts as a parent, and another set becomes
its child when it shows no enrichment of its own, both with the parent's genes removed from the
ranking and within the parent's genes (p > 0.05). The `mainPathways` keep their fgsea `padj`.
Survivors get `main = TRUE`; fry rows get `NA`.

```{r collapse}
main_sets <- map(set_names(contrast_names), function(contrast) {
  significant <- fgsea_raw[[contrast]][padj < 0.05][order(pval)]
  fgsea::collapsePathways(significant, sets, ranked[[contrast]], pval.threshold = 0.05)$mainPathways
})
lengths(main_sets)
```

```{r annotate-tests}
set_tests <- set_tests |>
  mutate(
    main = if_else(method == "fgsea", set_id %in% main_sets[[contrast[1]]], NA),
    .by = contrast
  ) |>
  left_join(
    select(set_catalog, set_id, database, pathway, source_size, description),
    by = "set_id"
  ) |>
  relocate(contrast, method, set_id, database, pathway)
```

## Set summary

Sets at adjusted p < 0.05 per contrast.

```{r set-summary}
set_summary <- set_tests |>
  summarise(
    sets = n_distinct(set_id),
    fgsea = sum(method == "fgsea" & padj < 0.05),
    collapsed = sum(method == "fgsea" & padj < 0.05 & main),
    fry = sum(method == "fry" & padj < 0.05),
    .by = contrast
  )
set_summary
```

## Figures

The figures show the four contrasts other than baseline.

```{r survivors}
shown <- c("BFR_Post-Pre", "HLRT_Post-Pre", "Modality_x_Time_Interaction", "BFR_Post-HLRT_Post")
collections <- unique(set_catalog$database[set_catalog$qualifies])
survivors <- set_tests |>
  filter(method == "fgsea", padj < 0.05, main, contrast %in% shown) |>
  mutate(contrast = factor(contrast, shown))
count(survivors, contrast, .drop = FALSE)
```

S1 shows each contrast's ten survivors with the lowest adjusted p. The size scale spans the whole
page so panels compare. Labels drop the collection prefix, so a stem that repeats within a
contrast (`GOBP_MUSCLE_CONTRACTION`, `REACTOME_MUSCLE_CONTRACTION`) gets its collection appended.

```{r survivor-figure}
labelled <- mutate(
  survivors,
  stem = sub("^[A-Z0-9]+_", "", pathway),
  pathway = if_else(
    duplicated(stem) | duplicated(stem, fromLast = TRUE), paste0(pathway, " ", database), pathway
  ),
  .by = contrast
)
panels <- map(split(labelled, labelled$contrast, drop = TRUE), function(contrast_rows) {
  top <- contrast_rows |>
    slice_min(padj, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    mutate(label = enrichVolcano::clean_label(pathway, width = 45))
  ggplot(top, aes(NES, reorder(label, NES), size = n, colour = database)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, colour = "grey75") +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.9, show.legend = TRUE) +
    scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Dark2", limits = collections, name = NULL) +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3))) +
    scale_size_continuous(range = c(1.5, 5), limits = range(labelled$n), name = "genes") +
    labs(
      x = "normalised enrichment score", y = NULL,
      title = sprintf(
        "%s, %d of %d survivors", contrast_rows$contrast[1], nrow(top), nrow(contrast_rows)
      )
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), plot.title = element_text(size = 9))
})
s1 <- wrap_plots(panels, ncol = 1, guides = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(title = "S1. Ten strongest collapse survivors", tag_levels = "A")
```

S2 counts significant sets per collection and contrast before and after the collapse.

```{r collapse-effect}
collapse_effect <- set_tests |>
  filter(method == "fgsea", padj < 0.05, contrast %in% shown) |>
  summarise(before = n(), after = sum(main), .by = c(contrast, database)) |>
  pivot_longer(c(before, after), names_to = "when", values_to = "sets") |>
  mutate(when = factor(when, c("before", "after")), contrast = factor(contrast, shown))
s2 <- ggplot(collapse_effect, aes(when, sets, fill = database)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  facet_wrap(~contrast, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Dark2", name = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "significant sets") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  plot_annotation(title = "S2. Significant sets before and after collapse")

pdf(file.path(stage, "b_reports", "01_run_fgsea_and_fry_figures.pdf"), width = 8.27, height = 11.69)
print(s1)
print(s2)
invisible(dev.off())
```

## Save results

Leading edges are saved `;`-joined.

```{r write}
write_xlsx(
  list(
    set_summary = set_summary,
    protein_summary = protein_summary,
    set_tests = mutate(set_tests, leadingEdge = map_chr(leadingEdge, paste, collapse = ";")),
    protein_results = protein_results
  ),
  file.path(stage, "c_data", "01_run_fgsea_and_fry.xlsx")
)
```
